C0.quote: every strategy-proof, anonymous social choice function can be described geometrically
C0.note: Voting rules (binary social choice functions) and their strategy-proofness.

C1.quote: φ ∈ Φ is strategy-proof if and only if fφ is dually monotone.
C1.note: Representation/characterisation of anonymous strategy-proof rules; the property is strategyproofness. Primary AX as characterisation.

C2.1.quote: based upon the profile P = (Pv)v∈V of preferences expressed by its members

C2.2.quote: it can be indifference between the two alternatives
C2.2.note: Each voter expresses a, b or indifference over two alternatives (weak order).

C2.3.note: Paper speaks of preferences; strategyproofness defined with respect to Pv as true preference (≻ with Pv).

C2.4.quote: profile P = (Pv)v∈V of preferences expressed by its members
C2.4.note: Preferences and inputs are the same object P; rule applied directly. Strategyproofness uses Qv as alternative reports but with the same notation type. No statement of sincerity; IDU chosen.

C3.1.quote: this agent can advantageously manipulate P (k + 1, m) by declaring indifference.
C3.1.note: The main analysis is strategyproofness, which considers misreports; no non-strategic main analysis.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions for voters; only preference-based manipulation.

C5.1.note: No welfare, efficiency, representation criteria in results.

claims.quote: To ensure a fair consideration of the opinions of all agents
